races.title: State House, District 55
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Clancy Baucom
cands.bio: Union County Republican who owns a wholesale nursery in Marshville, which he has run for 37 years. Appointed to the Union County Board of Commissioners in March 2024. Won the District 55 seat in the North Carolina House in 2026 and takes office January 1, 2027.

endorsements.text: Announced his campaign in August 2025 with the endorsement of the entire Union County Board of Commissioners.
Says he was the only primary candidate recommended by Grass Roots North Carolina, a gun-rights organization (claim from his campaign site).

cands.gaps: We could not find a birth town or birth year for Baucom. We found no reporting or records on his specific actions or votes on the Union County board, so his campaign claims about tax incentives, water supply and farmland preservation are unverified. We found no stated position on data centers, homestead property taxes, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, school choice or teacher pay, or police pay. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We found no news coverage or controversies about him.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign site calls him a native of rural Union County whose family has been there for generations, and Wikipedia calls him a lifelong Union County resident who graduated from Piedmont High School.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has owned and run a 200-acre wholesale nursery in Marshville for 37 years, and has served on the Union County Board of Commissioners since being appointed on March 18, 2024.
qual.why: Local elected office plus decades as a business owner fits the middle band. There is no record of prior state legislative service, or of law, policy or budget work.
qual.label: Local elected office plus decades as a business owner fits the middle band. There is no record of prior state legislative service, or of law, policy or budget work.

land-for-floridians.evidence: Says foreign enemies should never own American farmland and that, if elected, he will work to protect North Carolina farmland from foreign adversaries.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Says developers see farmland as a profit margin and that he wants to protect farmland from government regulation that could drive farmers out, and from development pressure. He also says that on the county board he has worked to ensure farmland is preserved.

second-amendment.evidence: Calls himself a proud gun owner who will support Second Amendment rights, and says he was the only candidate in the primary recommended by Grass Roots North Carolina.

pro-life.evidence: Says he will always stand for the unborn and support pregnant women in crisis, and lists supporting the life of the unborn among his legislative priorities.

cands.name: John J. Kirkpatrick IV
cands.bio: Democrat and member of the Union County Public Schools school board for District 1 since March 2021, when he was appointed. He won election to the seat in 2022 and again in 2024. He was the Democratic nominee for North Carolina House District 55 in 2026.

endorsements.text: Listed as endorsed in 2026 by the "Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy" voter guide (Sway voting group by Tevin (Momala) Davis), per Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: We couldn't find where he was born or raised, when he moved to North Carolina, or his career outside the school board. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022, 2024 or 2026, and we found no campaign website or interviews, so his stated positions are unknown. We found no records of his actions or statements on data centers, property taxes, development, land ownership, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or school choice. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or other endorsements.
